title: Compute Engine, GKE or Cloud Run
intro: Start from the operational contract you need to own (OS, cluster, or only the container), then check state, protocol, scaling-to-zero and team skills. "Managed" is not automatically correct: a constraint such as a kernel module, a GPU driver, or a long-lived TCP protocol can rule a managed option out.

matrix.requirement: Stateless HTTP container, spiky traffic, scale to zero
matrix.whyFits: No cluster to operate; request-driven autoscaling; revisions with traffic splitting [S057] [S058]
matrix.whenNot: You need privileged containers, custom kernel settings or node-level daemons
matrix.verify: Request timeout, concurrency, minimum instances, cold-start tolerance

matrix.requirement: Many microservices, Kubernetes APIs, shared platform team
matrix.whyFits: Kubernetes API with Google-managed nodes and per-Pod billing [S053]
matrix.whenNot: Workloads need node-level customisation Autopilot disallows
matrix.verify: Autopilot workload restrictions for your Pods

matrix.requirement: Specialised node configuration, DaemonSets, custom node images
matrix.whenNot: Team cannot staff node upgrades and capacity planning

matrix.requirement: Lift-and-shift VM, licensed OS, stateful single host
matrix.whyFits: OS-level control; MIG adds autohealing and rolling updates [S061]
matrix.whenNot: Workload is a stateless container with no OS dependency

matrix.requirement: Fault-tolerant batch at lowest cost
matrix.whenNot: Job cannot checkpoint or tolerate termination at any time
matrix.nearestAlt: Standard VMs with committed use discounts

matrix.requirement: Small event-triggered function
matrix.whenNot: Long-running or multi-endpoint service

failureModes: Choosing Cloud Run for a workload that needs a persistent local filesystem or long-lived non-HTTP connections without checking the platform contract.
Choosing GKE Standard "for flexibility" and then lacking the staff to upgrade nodes.
Running batch on Spot without checkpointing, so preemption discards hours of work.
Treating MIG autohealing as a substitute for application health endpoints.
verificationSteps: Write down the one platform constraint that eliminates each rejected option.
Check current Cloud Run limits (timeout, memory, concurrency) in the docs before committing [S057].
For GKE, confirm whether Autopilot permits every Pod spec you need [S053].
Load-test scale-out and scale-in, including cold start.

title: Choosing a database or storage service
intro: Decide from the access pattern, consistency need, scale and geography, and operations budget, in that order. Product names come last. "Global" and "relational" together point to Spanner only if you also need horizontal write scale; otherwise Cloud SQL or AlloyDB may be simpler and cheaper.

matrix.requirement: Relational, regional, standard OLTP, existing MySQL/PostgreSQL/SQL Server
matrix.whyFits: Managed engines with HA (regional) and read replicas [S176] [S177]
matrix.whenNot: Write throughput or size exceeds a single primary

matrix.requirement: PostgreSQL-compatible, high performance, mixed analytical reads
matrix.whyFits: PostgreSQL compatibility with a managed high-performance architecture [S179]
matrix.whenNot: Workload needs multi-region strong consistency for writes

matrix.requirement: Relational, horizontal write scale, strong consistency, multi-region
matrix.whyFits: Horizontally scalable relational database with strong consistency [S175]
matrix.whenNot: Small regional app where cost and simplicity dominate
matrix.verify: Schema design to avoid hotspots [S174]; SLA by configuration [S173]

matrix.requirement: Very high-throughput key/wide-column, time series, low latency
matrix.whenNot: Need multi-row transactions or ad hoc SQL joins

matrix.requirement: Document data for mobile/web apps
matrix.whyFits: Serverless document database with client SDKs [S182]
matrix.whenNot: Heavy relational joins or analytics
matrix.verify: Write-rate guidance per document and index

matrix.requirement: Analytical SQL over large datasets
matrix.whyFits: Serverless warehouse; partitioning and clustering control cost [S170] [S171]
matrix.whenNot: Row-at-a-time OLTP updates

matrix.requirement: Unstructured objects, backups, data lake files
matrix.whyFits: Classes by access frequency; strong consistency for object operations [S183] [S184]
matrix.whenNot: Low-latency random record updates

failureModes: Picking Spanner because a prompt says "global" when reads are global but writes are regional and modest.
Monotonically increasing keys creating hotspots in Spanner or Bigtable.
Assuming read replicas provide HA failover (they serve reads; HA is a separate configuration) [S176].
Unpartitioned BigQuery tables scanned in full by every dashboard.
verificationSteps: State expected QPS, data size, consistency and RPO/RTO before naming a product.
Check the SLA for the exact configuration (regional vs multi-region) [S173].
Run a schema/key-design review against the product best-practice page.
Estimate cost with the pricing calculator and record assumptions.

title: Pub/Sub, Eventarc, Cloud Tasks, Cloud Scheduler or Workflows
intro: Ask who controls delivery: the publisher (Tasks: explicit invocation of a specific endpoint), the subscriber (Pub/Sub: fan-out, decoupled consumers), an event source (Eventarc routing), time (Scheduler), or a process definition (Workflows: ordered steps with state).

matrix.requirement: Fan-out events to independent consumers
matrix.whyFits: Decouples publishers from subscribers; each subscription gets every message [S040]
matrix.whenNot: Caller needs control over which endpoint runs and when

matrix.requirement: Dispatch work to a specific handler with rate limits and scheduled delivery
matrix.whenNot: Many unknown consumers need the same event

matrix.requirement: React to Google Cloud resource events (e.g. object finalized, audit log entry)
matrix.whyFits: Routes events in CloudEvents format to targets [S047]
matrix.whenNot: You need custom ordering or replay controls beyond the trigger

matrix.requirement: Run something on a cron schedule
matrix.whenNot: Multi-step logic with branching and retries

matrix.requirement: Orchestrate ordered API calls with state, retries and branching
matrix.whenNot: Heavy data transformation

matrix.requirement: Poison messages must not block processing
matrix.whyFits: Moves messages after max delivery attempts [S044]
matrix.whenNot: Messages must never leave the main path
matrix.verify: Pub/Sub service agent permissions on DLQ

matrix.requirement: Strict processing order per key
matrix.whyFits: Ordered delivery per key in a region [S045]
matrix.whenNot: Global total order is required
matrix.nearestAlt: Single-writer design or a database sequence
matrix.verify: Throughput impact; failure handling of ordered keys

failureModes: Treating Pub/Sub as exactly-once by default; exactly-once delivery is an opt-in subscription feature with conditions [S043].
No dead-letter topic, so a malformed message is redelivered indefinitely.
Using Workflows as a data-processing engine.
Scheduler jobs without idempotent targets, so retries duplicate side effects.
verificationSteps: Make every consumer idempotent and test duplicate delivery.
Inject a poison message and confirm it reaches the DLQ.
Test replay with seek/snapshot where required [S042].
Confirm IAM for the service agents that deliver events.

title: Data processing: Dataflow, managed Spark, BigQuery, Dataform, Datastream
intro: Choose by processing model (streaming vs batch), existing code (Beam, Spark, SQL), and where the data already lives. Moving data to the engine is often the most expensive decision.

matrix.requirement: Unified streaming and batch pipelines with windowing
matrix.whenNot: Team has a large Spark codebase and no Beam skills

matrix.requirement: Existing Spark/Hadoop jobs
matrix.candidate: Managed Spark (Dataproc / Serverless for Apache Spark)
matrix.whyFits: Runs existing Spark with minimal change [S187]
matrix.whenNot: Pure SQL transforms on data already in BigQuery

matrix.requirement: SQL transformations inside the warehouse with version control
matrix.whyFits: Manages SQL workflows, dependencies and assertions in BigQuery [S189]
matrix.whenNot: Transformations need non-SQL code

matrix.requirement: Change data capture from operational databases
matrix.whenNot: One-time migration with cutover

matrix.requirement: One-time or continuous database migration
matrix.whenNot: Ongoing analytics replication

matrix.requirement: Orchestrate multi-system batch DAGs
matrix.whenNot: A few sequential API calls

failureModes: Rewriting working Spark jobs into Beam without a business reason.
Streaming pipeline without a late-data strategy produces silently wrong aggregates.
Composer used for a single scheduled query, adding cost and operational load.
verificationSteps: Document data volume, latency target and existing code base.
Test with representative late and duplicate events.
Check the current product name in the docs; several have been renamed (see K-conflicts).

title: Network connectivity
intro: Separate four questions: hybrid connectivity (VPN, Interconnect), VPC-to-VPC (peering, Network Connectivity Center, Shared VPC), service access (Private Service Connect, private services access), and egress (Cloud NAT). Then check routing (Cloud Router, BGP) and SLA topology.

matrix.requirement: Encrypted hybrid link quickly, moderate bandwidth
matrix.whyFits: IPsec over the internet; 99.99% SLA only with the documented HA topology [S149] [S150]
matrix.whenNot: Sustained high bandwidth or private (non-internet) path needed
matrix.verify: Two tunnels/interfaces per topology; BGP sessions

matrix.requirement: High bandwidth private hybrid link, colocation available
matrix.whenNot: No presence at a colocation facility

matrix.requirement: Private hybrid link through a service provider
matrix.whenNot: You need full control of the physical link
matrix.verify: Capacity options with the provider (K05: verify range)

matrix.requirement: Connect a few VPCs with low latency
matrix.whenNot: Transitive routing among many VPCs is required (peering is not transitive)

matrix.requirement: Hub-and-spoke across many VPCs and hybrid sites
matrix.whenNot: Two VPCs only

matrix.requirement: Centralised network administration for many projects
matrix.whyFits: Host project owns network; service projects use subnets [S165]
matrix.whenNot: Teams require fully independent networks

matrix.requirement: Consume a managed or producer service privately
matrix.whyFits: Endpoint in your VPC; no peering of ranges [S163]
matrix.whenNot: Service supports only private services access

matrix.requirement: Private VMs need outbound internet
matrix.whyFits: Managed outbound NAT without external IPs [S166]
matrix.whenNot: Inbound connections are needed

failureModes: Claiming a 99.99% SLA from a topology that does not meet the documented requirements.
Assuming peering is transitive.
Overlapping CIDR ranges discovered after migration starts.
MTU mismatch across VPN or Interconnect causing fragmentation or drops [S156].
verificationSteps: Draw the topology and compare it to the SLA page diagram.
Check learned routes on Cloud Router [S141].
Run Connectivity Tests for each critical path.
Validate MTU end to end.

title: Authentication, authorization, organization policy and perimeters
intro: Four distinct controls are often confused. Authentication proves who the principal is. IAM allow/deny decides what that principal may do on a resource. Organization policy constrains how resources may be configured regardless of IAM. VPC Service Controls limits data movement across a service perimeter even for authorized principals.

matrix.requirement: Grant least privilege for a task
matrix.candidate: Predefined IAM role at the lowest resource level
matrix.whenNot: No predefined role fits without excess permissions

matrix.requirement: Block a permission regardless of grants
matrix.whenNot: You want to restrict configuration values, not permissions

matrix.requirement: Time- or attribute-bound access
matrix.whenNot: Access needs approval workflow
matrix.verify: Condition attributes supported by the service

matrix.requirement: Prevent service-account key creation organisation-wide
matrix.whenNot: Legacy workloads still need keys (plan exceptions)

matrix.requirement: External workloads (CI, other clouds) call Google APIs
matrix.whenNot: Provider cannot issue OIDC/SAML tokens

matrix.requirement: Reduce data exfiltration from managed services
matrix.whyFits: Restricts API access across the perimeter [S110]
matrix.whenNot: Problem is over-broad IAM within the project

matrix.requirement: Limit which principals a policy can ever grant
matrix.whyFits: Bounds resources a principal can access [S113]
matrix.whenNot: Simple project-level restriction suffices

matrix.requirement: User access to internal web apps without VPN
matrix.whenNot: Non-HTTP protocols without TCP forwarding support

failureModes: Using VPC Service Controls to fix an IAM over-grant.
Enforcing a perimeter without dry run, breaking production pipelines.
Granting basic roles (Owner/Editor) for convenience.
Distributing service-account keys to CI systems that could use federation.
verificationSteps: For any grant, state principal, role, resource level and condition.
Run VPC-SC in dry-run and review violations before enforcement.
Use Policy Troubleshooter for denied access.
Audit key creation via audit logs.

title: Encryption keys and secrets
intro: Separate encryption keys (KMS: you control key lifecycle and access) from secrets (Secret Manager: stores credentials, versions them, controls access). Destruction and retention decisions are irreversible in practice; they belong in change-controlled runbooks, not exercises.

matrix.requirement: Default encryption is acceptable
matrix.whenNot: Compliance requires customer control over key lifecycle

matrix.requirement: Customer-controlled key lifecycle and revocation
matrix.whenNot: Requirement forbids Google holding key material

matrix.requirement: Store API keys, passwords, certificates
matrix.whyFits: Versioned secrets with IAM and audit [S124]
matrix.whenNot: Data encryption at scale

matrix.requirement: Supply your own key per request (Storage/Compute)
matrix.whenNot: You cannot guarantee key availability; loss means data loss

matrix.requirement: Retire a key version
matrix.whyFits: Destruction is scheduled and irreversible after the pending period [S115]
matrix.whenNot: Any data may still depend on the version
matrix.verify: Inventory of dependent data; scheduled-destruction duration

failureModes: Destroying a key version still protecting data, making it unrecoverable.
Secrets in environment files or source repositories.
Assuming rotation re-encrypts existing data (it creates a new primary version; old data stays under old versions until re-encrypted) [S114].
verificationSteps: Inventory resources using each key before disabling.
Test secret rotation in a non-production project.
Review KMS audit logs for decrypt calls by unexpected principals.

title: Monitoring, logging, detection and incident response
intro: Monitoring tells you a service is unhealthy; logs explain why; detection finds adversary behaviour; incident response coordinates people. Alert on symptoms users feel (SLO burn), investigate with logs and traces, and keep audit logs as evidence.

matrix.requirement: Page humans only for user-visible problems
matrix.whenNot: No SLO defined yet

matrix.requirement: External availability check
matrix.whenNot: Internal-only service without a reachable endpoint

matrix.requirement: Count events from logs
matrix.whyFits: Turns log entries into time series [S101]
matrix.whenNot: Application can emit metrics directly

matrix.requirement: Retain logs longer or centralise
matrix.whenNot: Logs contain data that must not leave a region

matrix.requirement: Who read sensitive data
matrix.whenNot: Cost/volume of enabling everywhere
matrix.verify: Enabled per service; BigQuery on by default

matrix.requirement: Detect misconfigurations and threats
matrix.whenNot: Need custom detection over logs

failureModes: Alerting on CPU instead of user-facing symptoms, producing noise.
Data Access logs off when an investigation needs them.
Excluding logs at the router that later prove necessary as evidence.
No postmortem, so the same incident recurs [S093].
verificationSteps: Fire a test alert and confirm routing to on-call.
Confirm audit log types enabled per critical service.
Run a tabletop incident with roles (incident commander, comms, ops).

title: Supply chain, deployment and rollback
intro: A safe release is traceable (provenance), gated (policy), gradual (canary), observable, and reversible. Rollback is a pre-built path, not an improvisation.

matrix.requirement: Only trusted images reach production GKE/Cloud Run
matrix.whenNot: No attestation process exists yet
matrix.verify: Policy mode (dry run vs enforce); break-glass

matrix.requirement: Prove how an artifact was built
matrix.whenNot: Builds happen outside a supported builder

matrix.requirement: Find vulnerable dependencies in images
matrix.whenNot: Need runtime threat detection

matrix.requirement: Promote releases through environments
matrix.whyFits: Delivery pipelines with promotion and rollback [S105]
matrix.whenNot: Single environment, simple service

matrix.requirement: Gradually expose a new version
matrix.whenNot: Change is a schema migration that is not backward compatible
matrix.verify: Canary metrics and automatic abort criteria

matrix.requirement: Recover from a bad release fast
matrix.candidate: Roll back to last known good
matrix.whenNot: Release included irreversible data changes

failureModes: Canary without defined abort metrics.
Database migration that makes rollback impossible.
Enforcing Binary Authorization without a break-glass procedure.
Images referenced by mutable tags rather than digests.
verificationSteps: Rehearse rollback in staging and time it.

In a sandbox, try to deploy an image that violates the configured admission policy (for example, one missing a required attestation); confirm the enforcement mode, exemptions and break-glass path. Test continuous-validation logging separately: a logged violation is not a blocked deployment [S111] [S209].
Check that deployed images are pinned by digest.

title: SLI, SLO, SLA, backup, RTO/RPO and cost controls
intro: An SLI is a measurement; an SLO is an internal target for it; an SLA is a contract with consequences. RPO is how much data you can lose; RTO is how long recovery may take. Backups protect against corruption and deletion; replication protects against infrastructure failure and may replicate corruption.

matrix.requirement: Define reliability target for a user journey
matrix.whenNot: No measurable user-facing signal
matrix.verify: SLI measured where users experience it

matrix.requirement: Contractual commitment to customers
matrix.whenNot: Internal service with no contract

matrix.requirement: Recover from accidental deletion/corruption
matrix.whenNot: Need near-zero RTO from zone failure

matrix.requirement: Survive zone or region failure
matrix.whenNot: Cost exceeds the business value of downtime

matrix.requirement: Be notified when spending rises
matrix.whyFits: Notifies at thresholds; does not cap spend [S065]
matrix.whenNot: You need a hard stop

matrix.requirement: Hard stop on spending for eligible services
matrix.whenNot: Services in scope are not eligible

matrix.requirement: Best-effort automated shutdown (sandbox only)
matrix.whyFits: Stops billable services after a delay [S066]
matrix.whenNot: Production data must survive; active commitments block it
matrix.verify: Accrued charges are still billed; resources may be deleted [S207]

tables.title: Time-based error budget, 30-day window (43,200 minutes)
tables.note: Time-based SLIs only. 30 days x 24 h x 60 min = 43,200 min; budget = 43,200 x (1 - SLO) bad minutes. For a request-based SLI the budget is a share of eligible requests: (1 - SLO) x eligible requests; for example, 0.1% of 2,000,000 requests = 2,000 failed requests. Do not convert a request-based or latency SLO into minutes [S092] [S208].

tables.title: Cost controls compared
rows: Stops spend on eligible services only; check eligibility [S068]
Stops billable services after a delay and can shut down and delete resources. It does not erase charges already incurred, and active or pending commitments prevent it [S066] [S207].

failureModes: Using 100% as an SLO, leaving no error budget.
Calling replication a backup.
Assuming a budget stops spending.
RPO/RTO stated but never tested with a restore.
verificationSteps: Compute the error budget for each SLO and confirm alert windows.
Restore a backup into an isolated project and time it.
Record budget thresholds and who receives notifications.

title: Prompting, grounding, tuning, evaluation and metrics
intro: Escalate in order of cost and risk: prompt design, then grounding/retrieval for facts, then tuning for consistent style or task behaviour. Evaluate each step against a fixed set with explicit metrics. Grounding addresses knowledge; tuning addresses behaviour.

matrix.requirement: Change output style or format quickly
matrix.whenNot: Model consistently fails the task despite prompt iteration

matrix.requirement: Answers must cite current enterprise facts
matrix.whenNot: Problem is tone or format, not knowledge

matrix.requirement: Consistent task-specific behaviour at scale
matrix.whenNot: Facts change frequently

matrix.requirement: Compare model or prompt versions
matrix.whenNot: No representative evaluation dataset

matrix.requirement: Classifier where false positives are costly
matrix.whenNot: Missing positives is costlier

matrix.requirement: Detect drift in production
matrix.whenNot: Batch model rarely re-scored

matrix.requirement: Filter prompt injection / unsafe content
matrix.whenNot: Risk is in tool permissions, not content

failureModes: Tuning to fix stale facts.
Evaluating on the examples used for tuning.
Reporting accuracy on an imbalanced dataset.
Relying on content filters while tools hold broad write permissions.
verificationSteps: Keep a held-out evaluation set and report metrics per version.
Check citation correctness on a sample.
Red-team prompts for injection, aligned to SAIF [S081].

title: Agent identity, tools, memory and evaluation
intro: An agent is a principal that acts. Give it its own identity, the narrowest tools, explicit memory boundaries, human approval for consequential actions, and an evaluation harness. Several agent-platform features are new and change-sensitive; items marked verify were not doc-verified in this pass.

matrix.requirement: Agent calls Google Cloud APIs
matrix.candidate: Dedicated service account or agent identity (verify current feature)
matrix.whenNot: Shared identity across agents

matrix.requirement: Expose tools to many agents in a standard way
matrix.whenNot: Single internal function call

matrix.requirement: Agents from different systems collaborate
matrix.whenNot: All agents in one codebase

matrix.requirement: Consequential or irreversible action
matrix.whyFits: Limits harm from errors and injection
matrix.whenNot: Low-risk read-only action

matrix.requirement: Retain context across sessions
matrix.candidate: Managed memory (verify current Memory Bank behaviour)
matrix.whenNot: Data must not persist (privacy)

matrix.requirement: Deploy and scale agents
matrix.candidate: Managed agent runtime (verify current product behaviour)
matrix.whenNot: Custom infra requirements

matrix.requirement: Measure agent quality
matrix.whyFits: Checks tool choice and final answer [S074]
matrix.whenNot: No test scenarios exist

failureModes: Agent with broad write roles exposed to prompt injection via retrieved content.
Memory retains personal data beyond policy.
No trajectory evaluation, so tool misuse is invisible.
Assuming preview features have GA guarantees.
verificationSteps: List each tool, its permissions and its worst-case action.
Inject a malicious instruction in retrieved content (sandbox) and confirm containment.
Check launch stage of every agent feature in the docs before relying on it.
